boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all three frozen records in the Chancellorsville Campaign [April-May 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates: Chancellorsville April 30–May 6, Fredericksburg II May 3 and Salem Church May 3–4, 1863. VA033 and VA034 lie inside VA032's frozen interval; campaign-wide loss tables and Sixth Corps totals span more than one engagement and must not be added or assigned. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Corps; the live field reads zero. Lee says the Union force at Salem Church was reported as one army corps and part of another under Sedgwick, and NPS says Lee detached two divisions from Chancellorsville to meet it. Sedgwick says he was told a column 15,000 strong from Richmond had occupied the Fredericksburg heights behind him, and that he faced vastly superior forces.
claims.rationale: Unit-level and reported figures differ in scope; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. NPS says Union assaults were repulsed with heavy casualties and that Sedgwick withdrew after dark. Lee says Anderson and Early drove Sedgwick toward the river and that he made good his escape and removed his bridges; Sedgwick says he withdrew under orders at 2 a.m. on the 5th.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's link to Hooker's abandonment of the campaign is campaign context.

No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Sedgwick's total also covers Fredericksburg II (VA034) and must not be assigned to this engagement or added to it.

open_questions: Early's, McLaws', Anderson's and Wilcox's accounts of Salem Church, Hooker's dispatches to Sedgwick and the revised Sixth Corps return remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Doubleday is an interested participant history (he commanded a division at Chancellorsville) whose figures partly rest on others' estimates. Lee's, Sedgwick's and Early's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXV, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
